instruction: Adversarial review of WP-SCP-022 slice 020D1 (SCP self-dogfood wrapper) at safety/bypass lens. The wrapper is the caller-side entry point that adopters will eventually use. Hunt for ways the wrapper could be bypassed, weakened, or manipulated to make policy enforcement non-effective. SPECIFIC ATTACK SURFACES TO PROBE: (1) Fork-PR bypass — the `if:` expression compares `head.repo.full_name` to `base.repo.full_name`. Could a fork PR somehow satisfy this equality? (e.g., is the comparison case-sensitive? could a malicious PR set both head/base to the same fork? could the expression evaluate at the wrong time?). (2) Pull-request event spoofing — `on: pull_request` triggers run with the FORK's GITHUB_TOKEN scope by default; verify this is correctly handled. The job-level `if:` blocks fork PRs entirely, but is there a `pull_request_target` event variant that could be used to escalate? Note: this wrapper uses `pull_request` (not `_target`), so the GITHUB_TOKEN is the fork's read-only token — any escalation requires sibling PR. (3) SHA-pin tamper — the wrapper pins at @9820489. Could a malicious PR modify the wrapper itself to point at a different SHA (e.g., a malicious branch with permissive rules)? CODEOWNERS covers `.github/**` (per 020K R2-SAFE-014) so any wrapper modification routes to @jrnb2024 review. Verify this is correct. (4) Branch trigger scope — `branches: [main]` ensures the wrapper only fires on PRs targeting main. Could a feature-branch-targeting PR escape the gate? Yes, by design — only PRs to main are gated; feature-branch-to-feature-branch PRs are not policy-relevant. Confirm this matches intent. (5) Permissions escalation — `permissions: contents: read, statuses: write`. The `statuses: write` permission allows posting to `repos/<caller>/statuses/<SHA>`. Could a PR exploit this to post fake status checks elsewhere? No — the `${{ github.token }}` is scoped to the calling repo. (6) Reusable-workflow trust — the wrapper invokes `jrnb2024/standards-control-plane/.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@9820489`. If the SCP repo were compromised at @9820489, the gate logic could be subverted. The 020J tag-protection + required_signatures hardenings (live since 2026-04-30 morning) mitigate this for tags, and the wrapper pins at a specific commit SHA which is immutable. Verify the trust model. (7) Renovate cascade poisoning — Renovate auto-updates the SHA pin on tag bumps. If Renovate's source (the SCP tag list) were poisoned, an adopter would pull a malicious pin. Note: 020F sets up the Renovate preset; it is not in scope for 020D1, but the marker comment is. Could the marker comment misdirect Renovate? Verify the comment is well-formed. (8) The wrapper has NO `with:` inputs. Default `scp_bypass: false` means break-glass is not available on this gate. Verify this is the intended posture for advisory-mode v1.0.0. (9) The wrapper has NO `secrets: inherit` (per 020B(iv)). Verify this is correct. (10) For SCP self specifically: SCP's own services.yml, waivers.json, and code paths will be evaluated by this gate. Are there any files in SCP's tree that would create false positives, breaking SCP's own development workflow? (e.g., files with shapes that match a deny pattern accidentally). Specifically check: schemas/*.json files (could SCP-R-002 accidentally fire on a JSON schema?), policies/testdata/*.json (test fixtures are inputs to opa test, but does conftest see them?). Any bypass surface, weakening, or unintended consequence is a finding. Per WP-SCP-022 §4.3. Return SonnetReviewResult JSON.
